ROUND validates truncated signed-16-bit precision separately from its documented identity range and avoids unnecessary scale overflow. CEILING handles nonzero quotient underflow. MODULUS validates finite operands, nonzero finite single-precision-range divisor magnitude (including subnormals) without narrowing Double values, uses truncating remainder to avoid quotient overflow/cancellation, applies divisor-sign correction, and refuses unrepresentable correction instead of fabricating a boundary. Typed results retain the first operand unit while arithmetic uses canonical internal values; errors preserve existing caches/source formulas.

Native availability controls show full paths and missing/invalid/changed/unsupported/cancel states with exact-key Retry/Unpin/Cancel.

Pinned loading validates regular local source metadata before/after reading, shares the 16-entry/32-MiB resource cache, caps a result at 32 source paths/10,000 masters/32 MiB declared retained cost, and refuses stale owner/generation/pins or incompatible palette changes. Separate retained budgets do not establish a total-RSS bound.
